historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: FY2027-FY2029 base ex-motorway blend (~4.3%) net of the motorway run-off; the historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward rate (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year CAGRs are off the FY2020 COVID trough (revenue -10%, EPS EUR2.20) and include the 2021 Cobra IS acquisition (EUR5bn+ revenue), so EPS 5yr 31.5% vs equity 5yr 8.1% diverges far beyond the 30% threshold; 3-year figures (revenue 6.5%, EPS 5.0%, equity 5.8%, owner FCF 8.4%) are the representative ones.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = CSV free cash flow (OCF - capex) less IFRS 2 SBC: FY2020 4,357; FY2022 5,739; FY2025 7,314 (pre-FY2019 rows are pre-IFRS 16 and already bear lease cost in OCF, so the CSV series is roughly like-for-like for CAGR purposes). SBC grew from 0.55% of revenue (FY2020) to 0.76% (FY2025), so the owner-FCF CAGR (8.4% 3yr) trails reported (8.9%) by half a point - a small but widening share of growth is paid in stock. FY2022-FY2025 FCF growth also leans on EUR1.4-2.5bn/yr working-capital inflows that the forward build does not perpetuate.

scenario_narratives.base: Vinci compounds the ex-motorway group at ~4% with modest margin expansion while the French motorway concessions run off exactly on contract (Escota 2032, Cofiroute 2034, ASF 2036) with zero residual value; airports, Energy Solutions and Construction are what is left to capitalise in 2037. The surcharge recurs once (2026) and the normal cash tax rate is 29.5%. Working-capital inflows continue only in proportion to growth (25% of the revenue change), well below the 2022-2025 run-rate, which is why year-1 FCF is below the EUR6bn guidance.
scenario_narratives.bull: Energy Solutions rides electrification, data-centre and defence spending at high single-digit growth with margin to ~11%; airport capacity additions (Gatwick runway, OMA, Lisbon) lift airport growth; French fiscal measures lapse and the transport-tax case is won; order-book growth sustains large working-capital inflows; Vinci keeps a toehold in French motorways after 2036 via new concessions and operating contracts.
scenario_narratives.bear: France's budget crisis makes ad hoc taxation on Vinci structural, the motorway concessions end on time with no successor role, Construction and Immobilier stay weak, airport traffic stalls, and the working-capital tailwind of 2022-2025 reverses to roughly zero. The 2037 group is a mid-margin contractor plus airports, capitalised at 13x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Vinci as an owner would: unlevered owner FCF on the whole group, SBC and the full lease charge expensed, working capital tied to growth rather than to 2025's windfall, the French motorway concessions treated as the finite annuities they contractually are (zero terminal value after ASF's April 2036 expiry), NCI taken out at what the minorities are worth rather than at book, and one EUR WACC for all scenarios with the risks carried in the flows and weights. The question the model answers is what the post-2036 Vinci - airports, Energy Solutions, Construction - plus ten years of motorway cash is worth, not what a perpetuity on today's 18% margin would be.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal mix: the 2037 group is capitalised at 16x owner FCF; every 1x on the cap is roughly EUR4-5/share
Working-capital capture: 25% of the revenue change vs a 2022-2025 history of EUR1.4-2.5bn/yr inflows - 10pp of capture is ~EUR8/share over the horizon
French taxation: each extra year of the exceptional surcharge is ~EUR0.8/share; a permanent +1.5pp on the cash tax rate is ~EUR6/share
Successor motorway arrangements: the base gives them zero; a 10% residual at concession margins (bull) is worth ~EUR5/share
NCI fair value is an estimate (EUR6.0bn vs EUR3.65bn book); airport M&A multiples decide which is right
Airport capex (Gatwick runway, Lisbon Alcochete in the 2030s) is charged as capex at 5.0-5.3% of revenue without a matching revenue uplift beyond the growth path

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments (IFRS 2) (567)' (DG.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:24170); covers performance shares and the Group savings-plan discount. No cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed (French plans settle gross), so sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 June 2026: 585,891,697 issued less 31,748,863 treasury = 554.1m basic, plus 6.42m dilutive (5.87m performance shares + 0.56m savings plan) per the H1 2026 diluted-EPS note = 560.6m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution too would double-count). Vinci is an active repurchaser (EUR2.0bn FY2025, EUR1.0bn H1 2026, 16.6m shares cancelled in 2025) so the flat count is funded, and the annual savings-plan issuance (~7.5m shares for ~EUR0.77bn cash) is more than offset by buybacks.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:39:30Z (Euronext Paris regular close, Friday; valuation written Monday 2026-10-26 before the open)
inputs.net_debt_note: Net financial debt EUR22,450m at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 report, Vinci definition: gross financial debt less net cash managed; EXCLUDES IFRS 16 lease liabilities of EUR2,983m, which are charged in the flows under lease treatment B). total_debt/cash are set so that total_debt - cash ties to the reported 22,450: cash = EUR15,564m cash and equivalents, total_debt = 38,014. June is Vinci's seasonal net-debt peak (EUR19,075m at 31 Dec 2025): H1 carries the final dividend (EUR2.2bn), buybacks (EUR1.0bn) and the working-capital trough that reverses in H2. The June anchor is used with the June share count so that the H1 2026 buybacks hit cash and count consistently. The only inconsistency is that year-1 (FY2026) owner FCF includes the EUR264m already earned in H1 2026 - about EUR0.5/share, immaterial, and in the model's favour.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at an EUR WACC. Bund 10y ~2.8% (Oct 2026) + 5.5% ERP x beta ~0.9 = cost of equity ~7.75%; pre-tax cost of debt 4.4% (FY2025 average on long-term gross debt) = ~3.2% after tax; weights at market: equity ~EUR60bn, net financial debt EUR22.5bn -> ~27% debt. Mechanical WACC ~6.5%; the house uses 7.0% for all three scenarios to reflect the blend of regulated-concession (6-7%) and contracting (8-9%) capital, which is 60/40 by EBITDA today but shifts toward contracting after the motorway expiries. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality, French fiscal risk and the expiry are charged in the flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost): the full IFRS 16 cash lease charge - EUR871m FY2025 = EUR761m principal + EUR110m interest (cash flow statement line 'Repayments of lease liabilities and financial expense on lease liabilities', DG.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:24341) - is deducted inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (1.28% of ex-motorway revenue, ~1.17% of group revenue rising to 1.28% as motorways roll off). Lease liabilities (EUR2,112m non-current + 737m current at FY2025; 2,237 + 746 at H1 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, consistent with Vinci's own net-financial-debt and free-cash-flow definitions. D&A for cash tax is ex right-of-use depreciation: 4,206 total less ~760 ROU = ~3,446 = 4.6% of FY2025 revenue (motorways 1,470, ex-motorway ~2.95% of segment revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (Gatwick and Edinburgh 50.01%-owned, OMA 70.01%, Cambodia airports etc.). NCI is charged ONCE, in the equity bridge, at an estimated fair value of EUR6,000m rather than the EUR3,654m book value at 30 June 2026: Gatwick 49.99% ~EUR3.3bn (GIP paid GBP2.9bn for 50.01% in 2019, EBITDA since up ~30%), Edinburgh 49.99% ~EUR0.9bn (Vinci paid GBP1.27bn for 50.01% in 2024), OMA 30% public float ~EUR1.3bn at market, Cambodia and others ~EUR0.5bn. Cross-check: NCI share of FY2025 net income was EUR372m, so EUR6.0bn is ~16x, in line with airport multiples. Book value would be EUR4.2/share more generous.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route) on the fully consolidated group, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the owner-fcf-adaptations (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). A formal sum-of-the-parts was considered and rejected because Vinci runs one balance sheet, one treasury and one tax group, and the engine supports only one flow; INSTEAD the one feature that makes a perpetuity on consolidated flows wrong - the finite French motorway concessions - is embedded explicitly in the driver paths. HORIZON: 12 years, FY2026-FY2037, so the terminal year sits AFTER the last French motorway expiry; the run-off is encoded as a remaining-network factor on VINCI Autoroutes (FY2025 revenue EUR6,738m, EBITDA EUR4,784m at 71.0%, Ebit 3,311, growth capex 565m): Escota (471km, ~12% of Autoroutes revenue) out February 2032; Cofiroute (1,100km, ~25%) out June 2034; ASF (2,731km, ~58.5%) out April 2036; ~4.5% (A86 Duplex, Arcour A19, Puymorens) non-expiring. French motorway EBITDA, capex and D&A are stepped out of the group paths at those dates and are given ZERO terminal value in base and bear (the state has signalled public operation or short re-tendered contracts at competitive returns; successor contracts are assumed NPV-neutral). The 2037 group is airports (Gatwick freehold, ANA/Lisbon to 2062, Kansai to 2060), VINCI Highways, Energy Solutions and Construction; group EBITDA margin consequently falls from ~18.3% (FY2030) to ~14.0% (FY2037) and the terminal cap multiple (16x) is set for that lower-quality mix. The driver paths are the sum of an ex-motorway group (FY2025 revenue EUR67,861m, EBITDA EUR8,723m = 12.85%, D&A ex-ROU 2.95%, capex 4.85%, lease 1.28%) and the motorway run-off; segment assumptions per scenario are in the narratives. EBITDA basis: Vinci's 'cash flow from operations before tax and financing costs' (EUR13,507m), which is before SBC and before lease cash, so SBC (0.75% of revenue) and the lease charge (1.17%) are deducted separately; FY2025 EBIT check: 13,507 - 567 - 871 - 3,446 = 8,623 vs recurring operating income 9,401 (which is before lease interest and includes equity-accounted income). CASH TAX on unlevered EBIT: FY2026 34% (French exceptional contribution extended by the 2026 Finance Bill; EUR449m = +5pp in FY2025), 29.5% thereafter (ETR ex-surcharge 29.0% in FY2025; France 25.8% blended with UK/Germany/US/Spain). The French transport-infrastructure tax (~EUR284m/yr, under litigation) sits in opex inside EBITDA and is assumed to stay. WORKING CAPITAL: Vinci carries a structural WCR surplus of EUR19.7bn (26% of revenue) and booked inflows of EUR1.4-2.5bn/yr in FY2022-FY2025 (Cobra IS advances, record order intake, +EUR675m current provisions in 2025) after ~zero in FY2016-FY2018. That inflow is bookings-driven, not perpetual, so it is modelled as a capture rate on the revenue CHANGE (25% base, +EUR470m in FY2026 vs +EUR2,496m in FY2025) rather than carried forward; this is the main reason the model's year-1 owner FCF is below the 'could reach EUR6bn' FY2026 guidance, which implies ~EUR1.1-1.5bn of WC inflow. last_fcf / reported_fcf are on Vinci's FCF definition (after all capex, lease payments, tax AND EUR1,318m net interest) less SBC; the engine's projected FCF is UNLEVERED (pre-interest) and discounted at WACC with net debt deducted, so year-1 engine FCF is not directly comparable to last_fcf (the CSV free_cash_flow of 7,881 is OCF less capex and excludes the lease payment; not used). Growth capex in concessions (EUR1,173m) and Cobra IS renewables (EUR852m Zero.e, guided ~EUR0.9bn in 2026) are inside capex. Buyback_cash is actual FY2025 treasury-share outflow (EUR2,002m), not the authorisation. FX: reports and quotes in EUR; fx_rate 1.0. PRICE: 52-week range 104.25-143.15; the stock sits ~2% above its 52-week low after the FY2026 FCF guidance cut, H1 motorway traffic decline and French fiscal measures.
inputs.equity_bridge_note: Matching-asset rule: EBITDA excludes equity-accounted income (dividends received EUR282m are a separate cash-flow line) and the ADP dividend, so both assets are added back. Equity-accounted investments at FY2025 book EUR1,995m (segment table, DG.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:24965; H1 2026 figure not separately disclosed in the extracted text). Groupe ADP 8% stake at fair value ~EUR900m (URD: 100bp move = ~EUR9m). NCI deducted at estimated fair value - see nci_treatment.

bear.narrative: French fiscal pressure becomes permanent: the exceptional surcharge is renewed again in 2027 and a structurally higher take (31%) persists; the transport-infrastructure tax is upheld and widened, cutting motorway margin to 68.5%, with motorway revenue flat in FY2026 and +1.5% thereafter. Ex-motorway growth 3% fading to 2% (Construction shrinks in France around the municipal cycle, VINCI Immobilier stays depressed, airport traffic stalls on fuel/geopolitics), margin stuck at 12.6-13.0% as Energy Solutions' M&A dilutes returns, capex 5.5-5.9% (runway and Lisbon obligations, Zero.e). Working-capital inflows largely stop (10% capture) as order intake normalises. Cap 13x on a contracting-heavy 2037 group.

base.narrative: Segment build: ex-motorway revenue +2.7% FY2026 (guidance: Energy Solutions mid-to-high single digit, Construction flat ex-FX, airport passengers stable; Fletcher Construction and All for One add ~EUR0.5bn), then +4.5% FY2027-28 fading to 2.5% by FY2036; ex-motorway EBITDA margin 12.85% -> 13.8% (Energy Solutions 9.5% -> ~10.5% as guided, Construction 6.6% held, airports ~63% with mix gain); ex-motorway capex 4.85% -> 5.3% FY2028-29 (Gatwick Northern Runway, OMA, Zero.e ~EUR0.9bn/yr, Lisbon design) easing to 5.0%. French motorways: revenue +1.0% FY2026 (H1 traffic -2.9%) then +2.5% (tolls 70-83% of CPI plus ~1% traffic) at 71% EBITDA margin, growth+operating capex EUR700m falling to EUR200m by FY2035, stepped out at expiry with zero terminal value. Cap multiple 16x on the post-motorway mix.

bull.narrative: Ex-motorway revenue +6% FY2027-28 (electrification/data-centre/grid/defence demand keeps Energy Solutions at high single digit organic plus bolt-ons; airports +5-6% as Gatwick runway and OMA capacity land) fading to 2.5%; ex-motorway margin to 14.7% (Energy Solutions ~11%, Construction 7%); the surcharge lapses after 2026 and the transport-tax litigation is won (tax 28.5%); working-capital capture 35% on sustained order-book growth. Motorways: traffic recovers, tolls +3%/yr, 72% margin, and Vinci retains ~10% of today's motorway revenue after 2036 (A154-A120, successor operating contracts) at concession margins. Cap 18x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25% because Vinci's most valuable segment depends on a single counterparty - the French state - that has imposed a dedicated infrastructure tax (2024), an exceptional surcharge (2025, extended 2026) and forced concession addenda within three years, and the expiry negotiations are in that state's hands. Bull cut to 25% because the bull case needs several independent things at once: fiscal relief in France, Energy Solutions margin expansion through heavy M&A, and an airport traffic recovery. Base keeps the concession expiry fully on contract with no residual, so the scenarios already bracket the expiry risk rather than leaving it to the weights.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
